text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

A survey of 900 business owners and executives by Dun and Bradstreet reveals firms have lifted their predictions for growth in new orders, employment, sales and investment during the first quarter of 1997. Companies also forecast a sharp rise in profits. These signs of corporate confidence indicate there will be a "mild recovery" in economic growth. Page 1.

The National Australia Bank, Australia's most profitable public company, has announced a record first-quarter profit of A$582 million. The result was earned in a period of intense home loan competition and interest rate reductions and was 14 per cent higher than the profit of the previous December quarter. Page 1.

Superannuation and investment house Prudential Corporation's major corporate restructure has paid off with the company posting a 42 per cent increase in new business for 1996. Prudential wrote $1.1 billion of new business last year, $321 million more than in 1995. Page 35.

Despite accepting terms for a $250 million takeover bid for Elders Australia Ltd, General Oriental Investments Ltd is preparing to take legal action against Futuris Corporation Ltd claiming Futuris breached a legally binding agreement. Page 36.

Lihir Gold Ltd has confirmed that co-discoverer of the giant Lihir gold mine in Papua New Guinea, Gavin Thomas, has resigned as director of the company and is expected to leave the company he has been associated with for 15 years, Niugini Mining Ltd. Page35.

Strong growth in gold-credit card numbers and the addition of ANZ Bank to its international debit card list has allowed MasterCard International to increase card numbers by 30 per cent in the year to September. Visa still leads in the credit card stakes in Australia, but MasterCard's 3.5 million credit cards in volumes 11 per cent to A$9.92 million. Page 52.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Outgoing National Australia Bank chairman Bill Irvine yesterday told the company's annual meeting that a decision by chief executive Don Argus to take a seat on the 14-member BHP board would be a boon for shareholders, claiming benefits would flow from alliances between Australia's biggest bank and its biggest company. Page 19.

National Australia Bank's announcement yesterday of a 14 per cent increase in first-quarter profit from A$513 million to A$582 million may break the record profit for an Australian-listed company. Analysts believe a full year profit of between A$2.22 billon and A$2.3 billion may see the NAB break its own record of A$2.1 billion for the previous corresponding 12 months. Page 19.

Days of intense negotiations has seen the directors of Papua New Guinea-based Highlands Gold advise their shareholders to accept a 75c-a-share offer from Canadian mining company Placer Dome. The deal will see Placer purchase Highlands' 25 per cent interest in the Porgera gold mine in PNG for $316 million and all other Highlands assets transferred to new company, Highlands Pacific Ltd. Page 19.

Equatorial Mining NL directors claim a report by Grant Samuel & Associates found the value of their shares to be between 36c and 47c each, and has therefore recommended that shareholders reject a 25c-a-share takeover bid by the AMP Society. Page 20.

Oil and gas company Santos Ltd announced yesterday it had discovered separate gas and oil fields in South Australia's Cooper/Eromanga Basins. The finds are located near existing infrastructure and means the company's $200 million South Australian exploration budget was money well spent, after last weeks' discovery of the Nephrite 1 gas well in the same area. Page 20.

The Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association has forecast a significant increase in spending on petroleum exploration and development in 1997, in keeping with optimism about strikes in offshore regions and buoyant world oil prices. Pag 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

National Australia Bank is on the way to beating the record it set last year for the highest Australian public company profit after revealing yesterday a 13.5 per cent lift in net profit to A$582 million for the first quarter of 1997. Page 21.

Pressured retailer David Jones has received a much needed vote of confidence from a major shareholder, a US-based fund manager, which has lifted its stake in the group to 6.63 per cent in recent days. Wisconsin Investment now holds about 22 million shares in the retailer. Page 21.

Gold fell to a new low of US$350 an ounce yesterday although corporate activity and speculation in explorers kept the gold sector of the Australian stock market alive. The Sharemarket's Gold index fell a further 15.8 points to finish at 1716, but analysts claim it could have been much worse had it have not been for corporate activity. Page 21.

Superannuation and Investment group, Prudential Corp Australia, has hit the A$1 billion sales barrier following a major restructure last year. Prudential's strongest growth came from the superannuation market which jumped by 42 per cent and its core insurnce business also increased by 15.3 per cent. Page 22.

BHP Petroleum and US oil and gas group should make a decision by the end of March whether to press ahead with the development of a A$2 billion-plus liquefied natural gas (LND) project which will harvest the Timor Sea's Bayu/Undan oil and gasfield. Page 23

Highlands Gold suitor Placer Dome has finally crumbled to the board of its takeover target and agreed to break up Highlands after the Completion of the Canadian miner's A$423 million takeover bid. Highlands's board yesterday recommended shareholders accep Placers 75c-a-share offer. Page 23.
THE AGE

National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus yesterday announced a 13.5 per cent increase in profit for the first quarter with an impressive A$582 million. The highlight of the result was a 14.3 underlying profit which Argus said was an indication of the bank's efficiency and ability to win customers. Page C1.

Shares in the small Perth-based gold explorer Desertstone NL rose 110 per cent yesterday following news of a possible gold discovery near Lake Torrens, north of Adelaide. The site is close to the under-explored Gawler Craton, an area Desertstone managing director Gerald Johnson says is the place to go for big deposits. Page C1.

New Zealand Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash has sought to dampen inflationary expectations in his first key speech since the formation last month of the centre-right coalition Government. Brash says the Reserve Bank will attempt to keep inflation inside the 0-3 per cent range by trying to have inflation as close to the middle part of the range as possible. Page C1.

A resolution between Papua-New Guinea-based Highlands Gold and Canadian gold giant Placer Dome appears to have been reached, with Highland's shareholders allowed to keep control of their prized non-Porgera mine assets in underwriting deal. Page C1.

Camelot Resources has raised A$10 million through a share placement to help fund the takeover bid announced yesterday by the company and Canadian Partner Teck Corporation TECa.TO for the Western Australian gold group Mount Edon Gold. Page C1.

Wholly owned subsidiary of AMP, Quay Mining, has had a setback in its 25c-a-share offer for a takeover of Western Australian explorer Equatorial Mining, with Equatorial directors unanimously rejecting the bid and advising shareholders not to accept its offer. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
